warning: A source commit token does not cover writers marked partial, pending or external. Do not claim full multi-file source consistency until they join the contract.

preparation.note: Whole regeneration captures one target/options, prepares outside the gate, compares dependencies and commits all generated artifacts plus settings/scope together. Cache adoption and compatibility notifications follow commit. Whole-regenerate now holds lifecycle ownership before target lookup/migration through source commit; create worker borrows the existing caller capability. Other artifact writers, defaults authority and total cache ordering remain partial.

internalJournals.note: Fixed allowlisted source record; prepared/committed/archived/compensating phases couple deletion decision to the canonical/legacy selection pair. Not an additional runtime snapshot field. Recovery reconciles validated Before/After archive bytes only and never retries directory removal.

sources.note: No in-repository producer found. ProfileManager.saveSettings writes WeaponX/settings.plist, a different path; it must not be claimed as this writer.

profile-create-completion.boundary: Create captures one explicit target/network packet, prepares inactive artifacts, saves metadata and conditionally activates settings/scope plus canonical/legacy selection. Lease and exclusive directory reservation protect cooperating producers; registry byte CAS and revision/proof checks reject stale state. Source writers/seed-zero stop at pending deletion decisions; load resolves validated H3C journal states before adopting committed selection and deferred defaults. Failed prepare has no selection effect; committed deletion can finish on reload, and external selection drift may cancel it by restoring only its own known registry bytes. Full directory cleanup, non-lifecycle artifact writers, metadata sidecar atomicity and defaults/security authority remain partial.

identifier-settings-scope.boundary: Stage settings and scope under one source gate; notify only after outer commit returns.

profile-lifecycle.boundary: Cooperating lifecycle/selection writers acquire nonblocking ownership before source transactions; raw registry byte/presence CAS rejects stale instances. H3C prepares secure validated Before/After archive snapshots before selection changes, commits fallback plus deletion decision in one source transaction, records archive installation, and replays or compensates known snapshots under lifecycle ownership before loading UI state. Pending/invalid intents block mutation. Recovery never rewrites selection or retries recursive cleanup; external unknown archives, remaining artifact writers, metadata sidecars, preferences authority and power-loss durability remain partial.

identifier-artifacts.boundary: Fixed-target prepare/compare/commit of enabled groups, unconditional WiFi, missing theme and settings/scope. One source commit; no provider/setter callback under source gate. Cache-only adoption and legacy battery mirror/notifications after commit; inactive target skips global cache adoption. H3D acquires lifecycle ownership before target lookup/migration through source commit; creation borrows caller capability without reacquiring or invalidating it. Root/directory/journal checks precede staging; owned batches release before receipt-checked compatibility callbacks. Migration/directory creation still precede generated-candidate rollback. Standalone artifact writers, legacy defaults authority and total cache ordering remain separate.

identifier-telephony.boundary: H3J freezes manual value/type, validates format before ownership, then acquires lifecycle before existing path/schema preflight, captures target/source basis once and holds pinned identity through regional DB preparation and paired sidecar/IDs/counter commit. Directory/root/pending-delete validation precedes staging; finally releases on success, early return and exception. Provider work remains outside source gate; dependency comparison still rejects bypass-writer drift. Non-iPhone manual compatibility, lowercase MEID spelling, regional policy and counter semantics remain unchanged. Preflight migration/path repair is outside candidate rollback; DB catalog generation and total cache ordering remain separate; model/software/cellular-refresh lifecycle joins in H3K and explicit/reader migration in H3M.

identifier-dependencies.boundary: H3K standalone regeneration/custom model/software/cellular refresh acquire lifecycle before target/schema preflight, pin identity through preparation and commit, and revalidate namespace/pending deletion before staging. Missing tuple software/cellular fallbacks pass the same mutation into a prepare/commit-only helper without nested acquire or publication. Release before compatibility callbacks, including fallback publication; finally covers returns/exceptions. Custom model input is copied, with original membership validation before acquire. Preserve owned-key replacement, legacy sidecar removal, dependency comparison, counters, value policy and existing post-publication fallback response read. Preflight migration/path repair remains outside candidate rollback. Pure batch/create preparation is unchanged; H3M composes schema preflight with the same parent lease. Defaults, catalog generation and total cache/response ordering remain separate.

identifier-values.boundary: H3I scalar/UUID/UDID generation, custom scalar, ATT and theme acquire lifecycle before existing path/schema preflight and hold scope through preparation/sidecar+IDs commit; directory/journal guards precede staging. Custom value/type detach before use. Release before compatibility publication/logging. Reader profileIdentityPath stays unchanged; completed legacy schema preflight is outside final candidate rollback. H3L uptime/boot compatibility wrappers acquire the same lifecycle scope, use generation-disabled reads, prepare a missing pair outside the source gate, and stage pair initialization plus requested scalar together in one source commit. Failure rolls back the whole pair without safe-default persistence or cache adoption; release precedes success-only adoption. Existing source precedence, date/seconds/display shapes and counter policy remain unchanged; H3M adds explicit owned/borrowed migration and coordinated cold-reader repair; existing-schema live readers remain outside the writer gate. Standalone telephony joins in H3J and model/software/cellular refresh in H3K. Serial retains policy delay/adapter. Cache publication ordering and mutable manager-state safety remain separate.

identifier-migration.boundary: H3M direct/current migration owns lifecycle; writer/batch callers compose a supplied lease through a borrowed pinned identity scope, without reacquiring or releasing the parent. Reader schema>=2 stays live-file fast path; cold reads acquire ownership, recheck selection and perform legacy repair only after pending-delete preflight. Scope validates directory/journal before one source transaction of legacy fields, sidecars, schema and single counter bump. Schema recheck remains inside source gate; explicit capabilities replace thread-local recursion bypass. Busy is nonblocking error12 and needs caller retry; exceptions close scopes. Repair/migration still precede candidate rollback; external namespace changes after checks, archive/directory durability and total cache ordering remain separate.

battery.boundary: H3H resolves canonical target under lifecycle ownership, borrows that lease for an existing identity scope, and commits battery_info/device_ids before the best-effort legacy global mirror. Standalone notifications require successful intended persistence and run after ownership release. No canonical active ID retains coordinated global-only persistence; invalid/missing target or unavailable namespace never downgrades to that branch. Read path is directory-effect-free; getter repair saves once. Cache-first values, generation policy and legacy/global read fallback remain compatible. Mirror failure after profile commit does not undo/report rollback of committed source. Global mirror is not a snapshot source; post-release mirror/publication ordering, process-exit convergence and mutable-cache thread safety remain separate.

network.boundary: H3E standalone saves, forced refresh and missing-data persistence acquire nonblocking lifecycle ownership before providers; target resolver runs once under ownership. Identity descriptor and profile proof are checked with pending-delete absence before source staging. Read hits retain the legacy read path without lifecycle/source lock; a miss rechecks the same active target after acquisition. IPv6 precedence and post-preparation merge are preserved. Source stages remain composable and do not acquire ownership. Failed ownership prevents generation; once generation starts getters retain their legacy candidate-return contract even if persistence fails. Other manager writers, caller UI generation before save and total reader/cache ordering remain separate.

wifi.boundary: H3G persistence warms optional ProfileManager outside ownership, then resolves manager-first/file fallback ID and captures cache under lifecycle ownership. Pins existing identity, validates directory and pending-delete state before one wifi_info/device_ids source commit; no directory creation. Generation/setter remain cache-first and can return an unpersisted candidate on failure. Reload clears old cache for missing/malformed targets and uses a validated filesystem path; observer has weak owner, retained token and idempotent registration. Manager-first authority, numeric/default fallback and pure batch adoption remain compatible. Stale manager memory across processes, whole-getter capture, mutable-cache races and total cache ordering remain separate.

uptime.boundary: H3F holds lifecycle ownership and pins existing identity through sysctl/preparation and boot_time/system_uptime/device_ids source commit. Missing/replaced targets and pending deletion reject staging; no directory creation. Cache adoption follows commit and ownership release; exceptions preserve prior cache. Pure batch preparation stays independent. H3L shares the sysctl/preparation-only helper with owned compatibility writers and adds generation-disabled read modes returning 0/nil on a miss; malformed scalar/date fields fall through safely. Existing public getter adapters retain auto-generation and safe-default behavior. Cache ordering and live read consistency remain separate; H3M guards IdentifierManager schema preflight, which is still outside candidate rollback.

storage.boundary: H3F explicit/current persistence acquires lifecycle before current selection and cache capture; current selection preserves canonical-file authority. Pins profile root itself, so existing legacy profiles need no identity child. Checks directory proof and pending delete before one source commit of the existing full storage record. Setters still mutate cache before autosave; separate setters and model/device_ids changes are not one transaction. Pure prepare/adopt, preference authority and concurrent mutable cache safety remain separate.

storage-preference.boundary: NSUserDefaults suite writes can flush after returning and rewrite the same tlink settings file; a lock around synchronize alone is not a complete writer contract.

dashboard-preview.boundary: H3N UI delegates to owned coordinator; freezes recognized preview strings, pins one identity, prepares tuple/model/optional storage outside source gate, then stages model replacement, name/serial sidecars, final tuple/counter and storage in one guarded source transaction. Storage merges only original three fields into legacy cache snapshot, preserving cache authority and extra cached keys. Existing successful name/serial plus final counter increments are preserved with overflow rejection. Short serial/partial DB tuple fail before writes. Cache adoption follows commit and release; callback exception cannot negate committed source. Prior create/switch/regenerate, scope/defaults writes and notifications remain separate phases; whole reset workflow, cache ordering, DB catalog authority and durability are partial.

security-store.boundary: H3O detached multi-key merges and atomic uint32 nonce use a standalone shared source transaction; nested high-level writes poison outer staging before mirrors. Corrupt source is preserved. Post-commit mirrors keep all three legacy suites and exceptions do not negate committed acknowledgement. Physical canonical preference domain remains writable by cfprefsd and unenrolled writers; source token is not full security authority or publication ordering.

security-direct.boundary: H3O Canvas detail multi-key writes, IdentifierManager Canvas aliases and nonce reset use security source transactions and notify only on commit. H3P routes IP monitor toggle/cache writes through the enrolled ip-monitor adapter. H3R enrolls region security packets and timezone callbacks through security-region-timezone. Other UI/indicator/metrics direct plist, NSUserDefaults and CFPreferences writers remain unenrolled; GPS/cache compatibility effects of region pinning remain outside the security transaction. Non-runtime keys still share the physical security plist; authority, compatibility mirror ordering and full migration remain pending.

ip-monitor.boundary: H3P observed IP and cache/timestamp merge in one detached security packet; cache-only saves preserve lastKnownIP. Toggle commits before start/stop, UI restores prior state on failure, alert confirmation requires success. stopMonitoring checks raw running flag and timer rather than the effective preference-dependent getter, so persisted disable still releases the timer. H3Q scopes callbacks to one start token; stop revokes the token and cancels tracked sessions, successful/error terminal batches finish their sessions, stale callbacks cannot publish into a later run. Weak timer/callback ownership and a retained weak reachability context avoid retaining or dereferencing a dead service. Void controls route to main; off-main persisted toggle rejects before writing. Endpoint, interval, throttle and consensus/fallback policy stay compatible. Malformed JSON types and missing data fail safely. Void cache APIs retain caller candidate-return behavior; defaults/cfprefsd authority, active-run overlapping results, transport/device integration and compatibility mirror ordering remain separate.

security-region-timezone.boundary: H3R validates typed geo/default fields and commits all region security pins plus conditional legacy network ISO in one detached source packet. Keeps optional source-IP/language omission, empty ISO and catalogue fallback policy. Toggle failure restores prior switch and suppresses three topics. Timezone callbacks publish only after shared source commit. GPS/cache writes and final sync feedback remain later phases, not atomic with primary security commit; their failures do not roll back that commit. Request/geocoder lifetime, stale callbacks, UI thread affinity, defaults/cfprefsd authority and mirror ordering remain separate.

preferences-daemon.boundary: Must settle canonical source authority and preserve legacy suite compatibility; cannot make cfprefsd acquire a private lock by wrapping UI setters.

upgradeWriters.note: Legacy preferences and ProjectX data migration run after stopping old daemon and before new publisher self-test; legacy binaries and concurrent manual commands do not join the new lock.

excludedAfterInspection.reason: Reads active selection to locate backups; inspected direct write calls are debug output, not these source plists. App container restore has separate transactions.

Read/render selection repairs now refresh memory only. Explicit name/description edits call the same-current-ID conditional metadata helper; their other profile display files are outside runtime source capture. Do not infer absence of transitive selection calls from direct-write inventory alone.
Writes its location preference, reads global scope; location data is not in this runtime snapshot schema.
